hardware: Raspberry Pi 5, Hailo-8, Debian 13, kernel 6.12.75+rpt-rpi-2712, GStreamer 1.26.2, HailoRT 4.21

method.h265: Main profile, ~2.35 Mbps, GOP30, no B-frames
method.pipeline_scope: RTSP -> decode -> RGB 640x640 -> Hailo -> pose decode/tracker -> payload construction

threshold.decision: pass when every stream reaches at least the threshold

decode_paths.h264: rtph264depay ! h264parse ! decodebin (avdec_h264, software; Pi 5 has no H.264 hardware decoder)
decode_paths.h265: rtph265depay ! h265parse ! v4l2slh265dec ! glupload ! glcolorconvert ! glcolorscale ! RGBA 640x640 GLMemory ! gldownload (hardware decode, GPU convert and scale)

conclusion.bottleneck: V3D GPU. At 10 H.265 streams the render queue is 94% busy while CPU is 67% and the same binary pushes 300 FPS through Hailo with synthetic input (10 test://ball streams at 30 FPS each).

gl_chain_alternatives_tried.result: Unsupported pixel format; glcolorscale only accepts RGBA texture-target=2D
cannot link; gldownload emits RGBA-family formats only
not run; its sink pad template requires format=RGBA, texture-target=2D

gl_chain_alternatives_tried.chain: v4l2slh265dec ! pispconvert (PiSP hardware convert and scale, libpisp 1.7.0)
gl_chain_alternatives_tried.result: caps negotiate, then Plane 0 buffer is invalid, 0 frames; reproduced at 1080p, 720p and 1280x704 and with system-memory, DMABuf and documented DMA_DRM caps

limitations: ENABLE_MQTT=OFF for the H.265 runs (native build); the H.264 runs used the rc3 image, where no MQTT connect or publish status is printed, so the broker leg is unverified in both.
H.264 numbers come from the rc3 image; an H.264 control run with the native binary at 5 streams measured 15.0044-15.021 FPS, matching it.
The H.265 11-stream decode-only run shared the machine with an unrelated container process at 81.8% CPU, so that boundary is conservative.
Source clips loop a 70-frame GMDCSA subject-4 Fall/01 encode; these are throughput results, not fall-detection accuracy.
get_throttled reported 0xe0000 throughout: throttling occurred earlier since boot, no current-state bit was set during any run.

artifacts.note: /tmp is tmpfs on this device; the logs do not survive a reboot.
